move: a torn-paper hole rips one collage shot away to a newsprint wall, then cutouts pop in one by one with 12fps stop-motion jitter
how: Two full-frame layers: shot A (teal paper, a gilded frame, torn text strips) underneath, shot B (a canvas-painted newsprint wall with mirrored headlines, body columns and white-out washes, plus an feTurbulence grain) on top, hidden by a CSS clip-path polygon. A 28-point jagged polygon grows from r=0 at 0.45s to past the frame by 1.45s on steps() eases, biased toward the bottom-left so it reads as paper peeled from a corner; a second white layer with the same polygon at 1.08x gives the torn white edge. Every cutout (sofa, statue-head figure with popcorn and ticket, cactus with sunflowers, two grey hands, phone, teacup, five paper labels) is an SVG or a text block wrapped in a filter that dilates its alpha by 7px, roughens it with feDisplacementMap and fills it white, so anything dropped in gets the cut-paper rim. Each cutout pops from scale 0 with a rotation and offset on steps(6) at its own time between 0.75s and 2.7s; the hands then pull back out. A jitter function, seeded per 12fps frame index and per element with fx.rng, offsets every cutout plus or minus 3px and 0.8deg, which is the stop-motion feel. Authored at 1920x1080 and scaled to the 1280x720 stage. Reference: NixMotion's Collage Art Promo (Motion Array), one 3.9s shot.
adapt: Swap any .cut's inner SVG for an of a real cutout (transparent PNG); the #cutout filter draws the white torn rim around whatever is inside, so photographic cutouts are the intended content. Change the label copy, colours and the newsprint headline list; reorder the pop schedule in the pop() calls. Keep the steps() eases and the frame-indexed jitter, or it stops being stop-motion. Drop shot A and start with the hole already open for a mid-film shot.
port: mount(el, shot) injects the two layers and the cutouts into el (unique the filter ids) and paints the newsprint canvas with ShotKit.rng; animate(el, shot, D) returns the gsap.timeline built here, with jitter(t) run from a single linear {u:0->1} tween's onUpdate over D instead of the seek hook. Scale the 1920x1080 root to the film stage (1x at 1920x1080).
caveats: feMorphology plus feDisplacementMap on every cutout is expensive; twelve cutouts at 1080p renders slowly and can stutter in live preview
clip-path polygons in percent are per layer; the torn edge is the white layer, not a stroke
the cutouts are vector stand-ins for the photographic collage elements of the reference
